subject: science

concepts.title: Atmosphere and Physical Presence of Air
concepts.definition: Air is an invisible, transparent fluid mixture surrounding the Earth that takes up physical space and forms an atmospheric blanket.
concepts.key_idea: Air is indeed present everywhere around us, occupies space, and is transparent.
question_patterns: is air present everywhere around us
how can you prove that air occupies space
what is the layer of air surrounding the earth called
why can we see through air
give one everyday example of atmosphere and physical presence of air

solution_steps.explain: An inverted open bottle pushed into water prevents water entry until tilted to release air bubbles.
The thin envelope of air extending kilometers above Earth's surface is termed the atmosphere.
Since air is transparent, objects can be seen through it, which is why the atmosphere is invisible to the eye.

concepts.title: Water Vapour in Air
concepts.definition: Water present in gaseous state within air that condenses into liquid droplets upon encountering cool surfaces.
concepts.key_idea: Atmospheric water vapour plays a crucial role in maintaining the natural water cycle.
question_patterns: why do water droplets appear on the outer surface of a cold glass
what is the role of water vapour in air
how is water vapour in air important for nature
find the significance of water vapour in the water cycle
give one everyday example of water vapour in air

solution_steps.explain: When air contacts a cold surface, contained vapour cools and condenses into liquid water drops.
Evaporated water vapour in air ascends and condenses to form clouds, driving precipitation.
The amount of water vapour in air determines humidity, which influences rainfall, fog, and dew formation.

concepts.title: Oxygen Component and Combustion Support
concepts.definition: The gaseous component of atmospheric air essential for supporting biological both respiration and fuel combustion.
concepts.key_idea: Oxygen supports both burning and is indeed necessary for living organisms to sustain life.
question_patterns: how will you prove that air supports burning
which component of air is consumed during combustion
why does a burning candle get extinguished under an inverted tumbler
what gas in air is essential for respiration
give one everyday example of oxygen component and combustion support

solution_steps.explain: Inverting a glass over a candle limits the supply of available oxygen inside.
The candle goes off once the limited oxygen supporting combustion is completely consumed.
The same oxygen that supports burning is also used by living organisms to breathe and release energy.

concepts.title: Nitrogen Gas in Air
concepts.definition: The most abundant atmospheric gas that does indeed not support combustion and remains after burning stops in a closed space.
concepts.key_idea: Nitrogen constitutes the major non-combustible part of atmospheric air.
question_patterns: which major gas in air does not support burning
what gas remains in a jar after a candle extinguishes
identify the non-combustible main component of air
what is the main constituent gas in atmospheric air
state two key points about nitrogen gas in air

solution_steps.action: examine remaining gas in enclosed jar
solution_steps.explain: Air remains in a container even after combustion ceases, demonstrating a gas that does not support burning.
This non-burning majority constituent is identified as nitrogen gas.
Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of air by volume, making it the most abundant atmospheric gas.

concepts.title: Carbon Dioxide, Dust, and Smoke
concepts.definition: Minor air components comprising gaseous carbon dioxide along with solid particulates released during fuel combustion and respiration.
concepts.key_idea: Carbon dioxide, smoke, and fine dust particles form essential minor constituents of atmospheric air.
question_patterns: why do we feel suffocation in a closed room with burning material
how can you detect tiny dust particles in air
why do factory chimneys extend high into the air
why are fine hairs present inside our nostrils
give one everyday example of carbon dioxide, dust, and smoke

solution_steps.action: pass sunlight through a small slit in dark room
solution_steps.explain: Shining light through a beam illuminates tiny floating dust particles dancing in the light path.
Mucus and fine hair inside nostrils trap inhaled dust particles before entering lungs.

solution_steps.action: explain smoke hazard in closed spaces
solution_steps.explain: Burning fuel in a poorly ventilated room releases smoke and carbon dioxide, causing suffocation.

concepts.title: Quantitative Composition of Air
concepts.definition: The numerical percentage breakdown of gases forming atmospheric air, dominated by both nitrogen and oxygen.
concepts.key_idea: Both Nitrogen and oxygen together constitute 99 percent of atmospheric air volume.
question_patterns: what is the percentage composition of nitrogen and oxygen in air
calculate the volume of oxygen in a given volume of air
find the remaining percentage of gases when nitrogen and oxygen are known
how much nitrogen is present in a volume of air
compute the answer step by step for quantitative composition of air

solution_steps.explain: nitrogen_percent and oxygen_percent combine to form the vast majority of air
multiply total volume by component percentage divided by 100
subtract the major gas percentages from 100 to find the share of carbon dioxide and other gases

concepts.title: Dissolved Air in Water
concepts.definition: Air trapped solution-wise inside water that provides oxygen necessary for aquatic organisms.
concepts.key_idea: Heating water drives out dissolved air as small visible bubbles before boiling starts.
question_patterns: how will you show that air is dissolved in water
why do tiny bubbles appear on the inner surface of container during water heating
how do aquatic animals breathe underwater
does boiled water contain dissolved air
how does dissolved air in water work

solution_steps.action: heat water in a glass vessel
solution_steps.explain: Gentle heating causes dissolved air to come out of solution, forming tiny bubbles on inner vessel walls.
Fish and aquatic life extract this dissolved oxygen for survival underwater.
Once water is boiled, the dissolved air is driven out, so boiled and cooled water contains very little dissolved air.

concepts.title: Trapped Air in Soil
concepts.definition: Air trapped within tiny pore spaces and burrows in soil that supplies oxygen to plant roots and soil organisms.
concepts.key_idea: Water added to soil displaces trapped air pockets, forcing soil organisms out during heavy rains.
question_patterns: how will you demonstrate that soil contains air
why do earthworms come out of soil during heavy rainfall
what happens when water is poured on a lump of dry soil
how do organisms living inside soil obtain oxygen
short note on trapped air in soil

solution_steps.action: pour water on a lump of dry soil
solution_steps.explain: Water enters soil pores and displaces trapped air, releasing visible air bubbles.

solution_steps.action: explain rain effect on soil animals
solution_steps.explain: Heavy rain floods subterranean burrows, forcing organisms like earthworms to come out to breathe.

solution_steps.action: link soil air to root respiration
solution_steps.explain: The air in soil pores supplies oxygen needed by plant roots and soil-dwelling organisms to respire.

concepts.title: Atmospheric Oxygen Cycle and Interdependence
concepts.definition: The reciprocal gas exchange where plant photosynthesis gives out oxygen and animal respiration gives out carbon dioxide, maintaining atmospheric equilibrium.
concepts.key_idea: Photosynthesis by green plants maintains the balance of both oxygen and carbon dioxide in nature.
question_patterns: how is oxygen replenished in the atmosphere
how do plants and animals maintain gas balance in air
why does atmospheric oxygen not get exhausted
explain the interdependence of plants and animals regarding atmospheric gases
describe atmospheric oxygen cycle and interdependence with an example

solution_steps.explain: Green plants produce oxygen during food synthesis via photosynthesis in excess of their respiration needs.
Animals consume oxygen and yield carbon dioxide during respiration, which plants then consume for photosynthesis.
This mutual exchange keeps the proportions of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere stable over time.

concepts.title: Wind and Applications of Air Motion
concepts.definition: Air moving continuously in a direction, called wind, which harnesses mechanical force for power generation and seed dispersal.
concepts.key_idea: Moving air drives windmills, assists aerial transport, disperses seeds, and powers water cycles.
question_patterns: what is wind and list its uses
how does wind help in operating windmills
list activities that are possible due to presence of air
how does air assist in seed dispersal and pollination
why is wind and applications of air motion important

solution_steps.explain: Air in physical motion across regions is termed wind.
Wind rotates windmills to pump water or generate electricity, enables flight of birds and gliders, and aids plant seed dispersal.

solution_steps.action: connect wind to weather and water cycle
solution_steps.explain: Wind carries clouds, drives evaporation, and helps distribute moisture, playing a key role in the water cycle.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the volume of oxygen in {total_air_volume} litres of atmospheric air given that oxygen constitutes {component_percent}% of air.

solution_template.explain: multiply total air volume by oxygen percentage divided by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the combined percentage of nitrogen and oxygen in air if nitrogen is {nitrogen_percent}% and oxygen is {oxygen_percent}%.

solution_template.explain: add nitrogen percentage and oxygen percentage together
